title: Tom Kha Gai
subtitle: Thai coconut chicken soup with galangal and lemongrass
excerpt: Tom Kha Gai is a Thai soup that sits between a broth and a light curry. Coconut milk is simmered with galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves to make a fragrant base. It is gently sour, mildly spicy, and deeply aromatic.
sourceNotes: Tom kha gai (coconut galangal chicken soup) is one of Thailand's most celebrated soups. Tom means boiled, kha means galangal. The soup uses galangal rather than ginger -- they are related but have very different flavours. The dish is found across Thailand and has been popular in Thai restaurants internationally since the 1980s.

content.text: Tom kha gai is one of the easiest Thai dishes to make at home. The key is infusing the broth with lemongrass and galangal before the coconut milk goes in. Do not rush this step. The lime juice goes in at the very end -- adding it too early makes it bitter.

items.prepNote: use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 2 stalks lemongrass -- bruised and cut into 3cm lengths
use galangal if available -- sliced into coins

content.text: Bring the stock to a simmer in a large saucepan. Add the lemongrass and galangal (or ginger). Simmer for 5 minutes to infuse.
Pour in the coconut milk. Stir to combine. Bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the chicken and mushrooms. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the fish sauce and chilli flakes. Taste and adjust -- the soup should be gently sour, mildly salty, and fragrant.
Squeeze in the lime juice just before serving. Do not boil after adding the lime.
Ladle into bowls. Top with spring onion and coriander. Do not eat the lemongrass pieces.

items.symptom: Soup tastes flat or lacks fragrance
items.cause: Lemongrass and galangal not bruised or infused long enough
items.fix: Bruise the lemongrass by bashing it firmly with a rolling pin or the back of a knife before adding. This releases the aromatic oils. Simmer for at least 5 minutes before adding the coconut milk.

content.text: Tom kha gai is one of Thailand's iconic soups. It is both a starter and a comfort dish. The key ingredients -- galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves -- are the flavour backbone of much of Thai cooking. The soup should be delicate, not heavy. The lime juice is added at the last moment to preserve its brightness.
